description: Experience the true taste of Liguria with Focaccia Genovese, a beloved Italian classic. This golden-crusted bread boasts an irresistibly soft, airy interior, perfectly infused with aromatic rosemary and rich olive oil. It is a simple yet profoundly satisfying treat, ideal for any time of day.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active and ready to work its magic.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, incorporating it until the dough comes together. It will be quite sticky.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a clean, lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Focaccia
instructions.text: Generously grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with olive oil. Gently punch down the risen dough and transfer it to the prepared pan. Using your fingertips, gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Drizzle with a little more olive oil.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Dimpling
instructions.text: Cover the pan with plastic wrap and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Once risen, use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough. Pour a generous amount of olive oil over the top, allowing it to pool in the dimples. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Bake the focaccia for 25-35 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and cooked through. The crust should be crispy and the interior soft and airy. If it browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven and immediately transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a final touch of fresh olive oil if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature, cut into squares or strips.

tips: For the authentic Ligurian taste, use a high-quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil. It is a key flavor component.
Do not skip the dimpling step; it creates pockets for the olive oil and salt, resulting in a more flavorful and textural focaccia.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it's baked. If you have leftovers, refresh them in a warm oven for a few minutes.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the sun-drenched coast of Liguria, Italy, right from your kitchen. Few aromas are as inviting as freshly baked focaccia, and fewer still capture the essence of Italian simplicity and flavor quite like Focaccia Genovese. This isn't just any flatbread; it's a masterpiece of texture and taste, characterized by a crispy, golden crust, a wonderfully soft and airy interior, and a generous sheen of aromatic olive oil. When infused with the fragrant notes of fresh rosemary, it transforms into an irresistible treat. If there's one bread that epitomizes the rustic elegance of Italian baking, it's Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil.

In this comprehensive guide, we'll demystify the art of making this Italian classic. From understanding its historical roots to mastering the dimpling technique, you’ll learn everything you need to bake a focaccia that transports you straight to Genoa. Get ready to impress your taste buds and your guests with the incredible flavors of homemade Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

Focaccia Genovese, or "fugassa" as it's known in the local Ligurian dialect, is more than just bread; it's a cultural icon from Genoa, the capital of Italy's Liguria region. Unlike its thicker, more rustic cousins found elsewhere in Italy, the Genovese version is typically thinner, boasting a distinctively crisp exterior and a light, chewy crumb. Its signature characteristic is the generous use of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, which contributes not only to its rich flavor but also to its unique texture and golden hue.

Historically, focaccia was a humble food, often baked in the ashes of the fireplace, serving as a simple meal for sailors and workers. Over centuries, it evolved into the beloved staple it is today, enjoyed at any time of day – for breakfast with coffee, as a snack, or alongside a meal. The dimples on its surface aren't just for aesthetics; they’re designed to hold pools of olive oil and coarse sea salt, creating pockets of intense flavor and a delightful textural contrast. This article will guide you through creating the perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil, a true testament to Italian culinary heritage.

## Ingredients You Need for Focaccia Genovese

Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil doesn't require an extensive list of ingredients, but the quality of each component is paramount. Here’s what you’ll need to gather:

*   **Strong Bread Flour:** High-protein flour (around 12-14%) is essential for developing the gluten structure needed for focaccia's characteristic chewiness and open crumb. All-purpose flour can work in a pinch, but bread flour yields superior results.
*   **Water:** Lukewarm water (around 105-115°F or 40-46°C) is ideal for activating the yeast.
*   **Instant Dry Yeast:** Or active dry yeast. Ensure it's fresh for optimal rise.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Incorporated into the dough for flavor.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO):** This is the soul of Focaccia Genovese. Invest in a good quality, flavorful EVOO. You'll use it generously in the dough, for oiling the pan, and as a topping.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Essential for our Rosemary Olive Oil variant. Fresh sprigs provide the best aroma and flavor.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt:** For sprinkling on top before baking, adding a delightful crunch and burst of salinity.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia

Making homemade Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a perfect loaf:

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour, fine sea salt, and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Knead (or No-Knead Method):**
    *   **Kneading:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
    *   **No-Knead:** If you prefer a no-knead method, simply cover the bowl and let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then perform a series of "stretch and folds" in the bowl every 30 minutes for 2 hours. This develops gluten without active kneading.
4.  **First Proof:** Place the dough in a generously oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Drizzle a very generous amount (about 1/4 cup) of extra virgin olive oil into a 9x13 inch baking pan (or similar size). Spread it evenly.
6.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the oiled pan. Using your oiled fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If it resists, let it rest for 10 minutes and try again.
7.  **Second Proof & Dimpling:** Cover the pan and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) during this time. Once risen, drizzle another generous amount of olive oil over the dough. Now, with oiled fingertips, firmly press down all over the dough, creating deep dimples. Don't be shy!
8.  **Add Toppings:** Scatter fresh rosemary sprigs and a good sprinkle of flaky sea salt over the dimpled surface, ensuring some salt settles into the oil-filled dimples.
9.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the edges are crispy.
10. **Cool:** Carefully remove the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil from the pan immediately and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy.

## Pro Tips for the Best Focaccia Genovese Results

Mastering Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil isn't hard, but a few pro tips can elevate your results from good to absolutely sublime:

*   **Don't Skimp on Olive Oil:** This is perhaps the most crucial tip. Focaccia Genovese demands a generous amount of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. It contributes to the flavor, crispness, and overall texture. Oil the pan, oil the dough, and oil your fingers!
*   **High Hydration is Key:** Focaccia dough is typically very wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add more flour, as this high hydration is what gives the focaccia its characteristic airy, open crumb and tenderness.
*   **Gentle Handling:** Once the dough has risen, handle it gently to preserve the air bubbles that have formed. This is especially important when transferring it to the pan and stretching it out.
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling, don't be afraid to press firmly, almost to the bottom of the pan. These dimples are crucial for holding the olive oil and salt, creating those irresistible pockets of flavor.
*   **Patience with Proofing:** Allow your dough ample time to rise. A slow, warm rise develops better flavor and a lighter texture. Don't rush it.
*   **Hot Oven, Short Bake:** Focaccia bakes best in a hot oven, which helps create that desirable crispy crust while keeping the interior soft.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** While dried rosemary can be used, fresh rosemary is incomparable for its aromatic oils and vibrant flavor.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Pay attention to how your dough feels. If it’s too resistant when stretching, let it rest a few more minutes.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Homemade Focaccia

Once you pull your golden, aromatic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil from the oven, the possibilities are endless. It's incredibly versatile and delicious on its own, but here are some serving suggestions to truly savor its flavors:

*   **Alongside Meals:** It makes a fantastic accompaniment to Italian soups like minestrone, hearty stews, or a simple green salad. Its ability to soak up sauces is unparalleled.
*   **With Dips:** Serve it with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping, perhaps with a splash of balsamic vinegar. Pesto or a white bean dip also pair wonderfully.
*   **Charcuterie Board:** Cut into squares, it’s a perfect addition to a cheese and charcuterie board, complementing cured meats and various cheeses.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally to create incredible sandwiches. Fill it with prosciutto and mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or a classic Caprese combination.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** In Genoa, focaccia is often enjoyed for breakfast, dipped in coffee! It also makes a delightful mid-afternoon snack.
*   **Appetizer:** Serve warm, cut into strips or squares, as a simple yet elegant appetizer for any gathering.

## Variations and Substitutions for Focaccia

While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a star in itself, the beauty of focaccia lies in its adaptability. Here are a few variations and substitutions you can try to customize your loaf:

*   **Different Toppings:**
    *   **Olives:** Black or green olives, pitted and halved, pressed into the dough.
    *   **Cherry Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes, pressed into the dimples, burst with flavor when baked.
    *   **Onions:** Thinly sliced red or yellow onions, caramelized slightly before baking or added raw for a sharper bite.
    *   **Garlic:** Thinly sliced garlic cloves, added with the rosemary, for an extra aromatic kick.
    *   **Other Herbs:** Thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs can be used instead of or in addition to rosemary.
    *   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added in the last few minutes of baking.
*   **Flour Blends:**
    *   **Semolina:** Replace 10-20% of the bread flour with fine semolina flour for a slightly coarser texture and a beautiful golden color.
    *   **Whole Wheat:** Incorporate a small amount of whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor and added fiber, but don't go overboard, or the focaccia might become too dense.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** While less common for Genovese style, some regions make sweet focaccia. You could try adding grapes, a sprinkle of sugar, and a dash of anise seeds for a unique dessert focaccia.
*   **No-Knead Focaccia:** As mentioned in the instructions, a no-knead method involving several stretch-and-fold cycles over a few hours can yield an incredibly open and airy crumb with minimal effort. This is perfect for busy bakers.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While this recipe is not gluten-free, many excellent gluten-free flour blends are available that can be adapted for focaccia, though the texture will be different.

Baking Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is an experience that engages all your senses – the feel of the dough, the intoxicating aroma filling your kitchen, and finally, the incredible taste of a freshly baked masterpiece. This iconic Italian bread, with its simple yet profound flavors, is a testament to the idea that the best food often comes from the purest ingredients and a touch of passion. So, roll up your sleeves, gather your ingredients, and embrace the simple pleasure of baking and sharing your homemade Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. Buon appetito!
